title: One In, One Out
idea: A function takes each input to exactly one output, and f(3) means the output when the input is 3.
misconceptions: Treats f(x) as f × x, so a factor inside the bracket comes out
Squares the minus sign too: −x² is −(x²), not (−x)²
Answers with the output when the input is asked for (e.g. a height when a time is asked)
Interprets P(0) as 'zero population' instead of the initial value

estimate.basis: 150 spoken words a minute, plus each pause, 0.8 s for each cue and 2 s for each tap question with its longer feedback line. The two figures are the two recall versions. Player turns are player-paced and not counted.

notes: Builds on ex.foundations.pre-substitute (Tess), so the recall uses Rook's tin-can-tess.watched and tin-can-tess.not-watched lines with his own short-version. Evaluating f(a) is substitution with a name on it, which is the whole link.

No second-method section: the map lists no methods. Of the skills' methods, direct substitution is the lesson, solve-for-input is example 3(c), and reading a graph or table and the GDC are left to later explainers (ex.functions.how-high-and-where).

The first misconception (f(x) as f × x) is the spot-the-slip, written as f(2) + f(3) = f(5). The −x² misconception is example 2's fill. 'Output when the input is asked for' is example 3(c)'s why question, and 'P(0) as zero' is example 3(a).
The terms are input and output (a pair, defined together), function and the notation f(x). The picture of a machine with an input and an output is the relay in the cold open.
The turns use fn-evaluate-function (situation basic-function). Its live numbers come from the engine, and the fallbacks are fixed and worked below.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Signal Tower, this is Rook. At the top of the mast there's a relay, and it does the same thing to every signal it gets.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: It squares the signal, takes away four, and sends what's left out to the settlements.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: A runner's brought up minus three. What goes out? Over.

board.write: Relay: square it, then − 4. In: −3. Out: ?

watched.speaker: rook-dead-air
watched.say: Before we go on air, a quick check. Tap one.

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Ten. Minus three in brackets, squared, is nine, and one more is ten. Keep those brackets. We need them today.
right.caption: Ten. (−3)² is 9, and one more is ten. Keep those brackets. We need them today.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Minus three goes in inside brackets. Minus three times minus three is plus nine. Add one, and it's ten. Keep those brackets. We need them today.
not_yet.caption: −3 goes in inside brackets. (−3) × (−3) is +9. Add one, and it's ten. Keep those brackets. We need them today.

not_watched.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_watched.say: Before we go on air, a quick check. Tap one.

not_watched.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_watched.say: Wherever the letter is, put the value in, inside brackets. Minus three in brackets, squared, is minus three times minus three. That's plus nine. Add one. Ten.
not_watched.caption: Wherever the letter is, put the value in, inside brackets. (−3)² is (−3) × (−3). That's +9. Add one. Ten.

not_watched.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_watched.say: Keep those brackets. We need them today.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Here's the relay. The signal comes in on the left and goes out on the right, and what happens in between is the rule.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: What goes in is the input. What comes out is the output. I'll use those two words all lesson, and I won't swap them. Swap them on air and a message goes to the wrong settlement.

board.write: input: what goes in.   output: what comes out

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Minus three goes in. In brackets, squared, nine. Take away four. Five goes out.
beats.caption: −3 goes in. In brackets, squared, 9. Take away four. Five goes out.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Send minus three again tomorrow, and five goes out again. Every time. Each input gives exactly one output. That's a function.

board.write: function: each input gives exactly one output

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: My oupa had a radio where one spot on the dial gave you two stations at once. Rugby and the news, on top of each other. One input, two outputs. That's no function.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: On paper we give the machine a name, f, and write its rule. f of x equals x squared minus four.
beats.caption: On paper we give the machine a name, f, and write its rule. f(x) = x² − 4.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: f of x means the output when the input is x. So f of minus three is the output when minus three goes in, and the input goes in brackets, and the rule runs on it, and out comes five. Sorry. Back on frequency.
beats.caption: f(x) means the output when the input is x. So f(−3) is the output when −3 goes in, and the input goes in brackets, and the rule runs on it, and out comes five. Sorry. Back on frequency.

board.write: f(x): the output when the input is x

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: One warning. Those brackets aren't a times. f of three isn't f times three. It's the name of the machine, then its input.
beats.caption: One warning. Those brackets aren't a times. f(3) isn't f × 3. It's the name of the machine, then its input.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: On paper now. Step one: what we're finding. f of minus four, the output when the input is minus four.
beats.caption: On paper now. Step one: what we're finding. f(−4), the output when the input is −4.

board.write: Find f(−4): the output when the input is −4.
board.label: Step 1: what are we finding?

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step two: the rule, before any numbers. f of x equals six minus two x.
beats.caption: Step two: the rule, before any numbers. f(x) = 6 − 2x.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step three: substitute. Every x becomes minus four, inside brackets.
beats.caption: Step three: substitute. Every x becomes −4, inside brackets.

choices: So the 2 multiplies all of −4, sign included
Brackets show the input is negative

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Copy that. Two lots of minus four, sign and all.
right.caption: Copy that. 2(−4), sign and all.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Without brackets, six minus two minus four looks like a subtraction. The two has to multiply all of minus four, sign included.
not_yet.caption: Without brackets, 6 − 2 − 4 looks like a subtraction. The two has to multiply all of −4, sign included.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step four: evaluate. Two lots of minus four is minus eight. Six take away minus eight is fourteen.
beats.caption: Step four: evaluate. 2(−4) is −8. 6 − (−8) is 14.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step five: say it. f of minus four is fourteen. Input minus four, output fourteen.
beats.caption: Step five: say it. f(−4) = 14. Input −4, output 14.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check: a negative input makes minus two x positive, so the output should be more than six. Fourteen is.
beats.caption: Check: a negative input makes −2x positive, so the output should be more than six. Fourteen is.

intro.speaker: rook-dead-air
intro.say: Your channel. Rule first, input in brackets, then evaluate. Over.

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Loud and clear. Input, output, and you kept them apart.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Put the input in brackets first, then multiply. Come in again.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Check the sign. A positive times a negative is negative, and taking a negative away adds.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: One thing harder. A square, with a minus in front of it. h of x equals five minus x squared. Find h of minus two.
beats.caption: One thing harder. A square, with a minus in front of it. h(x) = 5 − x². Find h(−2).

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: In x squared, the square belongs to x. Not to the minus. So the input gets squared first, and then it's taken away.
beats.caption: In x², the square belongs to x. Not to the minus. So the input gets squared first, and then it's taken away.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: You do the substitution. I'll keep the channel open.

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: One. Minus two in brackets, squared, is four, and five take away four is one. Lekker.
right.caption: One. (−2)² is 4, and 5 − 4 is 1. Lekker.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Square the input first: minus two in brackets, squared, is plus four. Then take it away from five. One.
not_yet.caption: Square the input first: (−2)² is +4. Then take it away from five. One.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Written out: five minus four, one. h of minus two is one.
beats.caption: Written out: 5 − 4, 1. h(−2) = 1.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check: x squared is never negative, so h of x can never be more than five. One is under five. Out.
beats.caption: Check: x² is never negative, so h(x) can never be more than five. One is under five. Out.

problem.setup: The charge in the tower's battery bank, as a percentage, t hours after sunrise is modelled by C(t) = 20 + 12t, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6.

parts.text: Write down C(0), and interpret it in context.
Find the time when the battery bank is at 74% charge.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Now the way an exam sets it. The tower runs on a battery bank, and a solar panel charges it through the day.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The charge, as a percentage, t hours after sunrise, is C of t equals twenty plus twelve t. The model holds from zero to six hours.
beats.caption: The charge, as a percentage, t hours after sunrise, is C(t) = 20 + 12t. The model holds from zero to six hours.

board.write: t = hours after sunrise.  C = charge, %

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part a. Write down C of zero. Zero hours, so sunrise. Twenty plus zero is twenty.
beats.caption: Part a. Write down C(0). Zero hours, so sunrise. 20 + 0 = 20.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Then say what it means. C of zero isn't zero charge. It's the charge at the start: twenty percent at sunrise.
beats.caption: Then say what it means. C(0) isn't zero charge. It's the charge at the start: 20% at sunrise.

board.write: At sunrise the battery bank holds 20% charge.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part b. Find C of five. Five goes in for t. Twelve fives are sixty, and twenty more is eighty. Eighty percent, five hours after sunrise.
beats.caption: Part b. Find C(5). Five goes in for t. Twelve fives are sixty, and twenty more is eighty. 80%, five hours after sunrise.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part c. The time when it's at seventy-four percent.
beats.caption: Part c. The time when it's at 74%.

ask.prompt: In part c, is 74 an input or an output?

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Output. Seventy-four is a charge, so it's C of t. The time is the input, and that's what they want.
right.caption: Output. Seventy-four is a charge, so it's C(t). The time is the input, and that's what they want.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Crossed wire. Seventy-four is a charge, and charge is what comes out. So C of t is seventy-four, and t is what you're finding.
not_yet.caption: Crossed wire. Seventy-four is a charge, and charge is what comes out. So C(t) = 74, and t is what you're finding.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: So set the output to seventy-four and solve for the input. Take twenty off both sides. Fifty-four equals twelve t. Divide by twelve. t is four point five.
beats.caption: So set the output to seventy-four and solve for the input. Take twenty off both sides. 54 = 12t. Divide by twelve. t = 4.5.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: In words: four and a half hours after sunrise. That's inside zero to six, so the model holds there.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check: twelve lots of four point five is fifty-four, and twenty more is seventy-four. Out.
beats.caption: Check: 12 × 4.5 = 54, and twenty more is seventy-four. Out.
